solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Disciple along with king in difficult situation

indicators.note: the words for 'along with king' are placed inside the word for a difficult situation

parts.note: to be in a stew is to be in a fix or difficult situation
along with means and
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A follower of Jesus, together with a monarch, finds himself in a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Andrew was one of the twelve apostles, the disciples of Jesus.

clue.text: Nothing said where ancient Greeks met

indicators.note: said signals that the word for nothing is spoken, giving the sound of the entry

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: Nobody speaks about the place where the Greeks of antiquity assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: The P is silent, so the hill's name is pronounced like 'nix'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pnyx was the hill in Athens where the democratic assembly gathered.

clue.text: Fix match yet again

definitions.meaning: to fix something broken is to mend it
to put two together as a pair once more

explanation.surface: Arrange a rematch of a game once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Mending something is the everyday sense; split with a hyphen, the word means pairing up again.

clue.text: Persuade last couple of people to prop up short rail

indicators.note: in a down entry, propping up means sitting underneath, so this piece comes after
short means the final letter of the word for rail is cut off

parts.note: to rail against something is to inveigh against it

indicators.note: the last couple of letters of the word people are taken

explanation.surface: Talk the final pair of folk into supporting a rail that is too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' is a verb, to rant, not a bar or track.
explanation.definitionFit: To inveigle someone is to coax or cajole them into doing something, a synonym of persuade.

clue.text: Poor admirer about to accept fine

indicators.note: about signals that the word for admirer turns round

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An impoverished supporter is going to take a penalty payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like a penalty but is the letter F; 'Poor' means shoddy, not impoverished.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky, uncool or of poor quality.

clue.text: Took tea that you didn't expect

parts.note: took means got, as in received
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone drank a cuppa that came as a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is shouted when catching someone out with something unexpected, a surprise or trick.

clue.text: Outstanding heavyweight entering now

indicators.note: entering means the heavyweight word goes inside the word for outstanding

parts.note: ace means excellent or outstanding
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A superb heavy boxer is stepping into the ring right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, without delay: a direct synonym phrase.

clue.text: Plug a vulgar dwelling

parts.note: a bung is a stopper or plug
low means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: Advertise a coarse house.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey house, a kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Getting overdrawn, blew out perfect society

indicators.note: out means the letters of the two words are knocked out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone running up an overdraft squandered their chance of an ideal community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blew out' looks like a phrasal verb; 'out' alone is the anagram signal for OVERDRAWN BLEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley's novel title is used ironically for a supposedly ideal, utopian society.

clue.text: Detach, having lost core operating system

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for detach is removed

parts.note: to unfix something is to detach it

explanation.surface: Disconnect a computer's software after its heart has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Unix is a well-known computer operating system, developed at Bell Labs.

clue.text: Fast vehicle escaping from shell

indicators.note: the vehicle word leaves the word for shell

parts.note: a carapace is the hard shell of a turtle or crab
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A speedy car breaks free of its outer casing.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning quickly, at speed.

clue.text: Government department beginning to consider current points of interest

parts.note: FO is the Foreign Office, a UK government department

indicators.note: the beginning of the word consider gives its first letter

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A ministry starting to weigh up present matters of concern.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci, plural of focus, are centres of attention or interest.

clue.text: On banks of Tiber, reluctant to cross

indicators.note: the banks are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of Tiber

parts.note: averse means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Standing beside Rome's river, someone hesitates to go over it.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across or go over something.

clue.text: Roman cardinals stifling a sound

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the cardinals surround the letter a

parts.note: V, L, I and D are Roman numerals, cardinal numbers 5, 50, 1 and 500

explanation.surface: Princes of the Church in Rome are muffling a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests churchmen but means cardinal numbers; 'sound' is the adjective, not a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is a valid one: logically well-founded.

clue.text: Briefly relevant to European

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: germane means relevant or pertinent

explanation.surface: Something pertinent, in short, about a person from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A German comes from Germany, a European country, so is an example of a European.

clue.text: Entangle party line

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Mix up the guest list or the schedule for a dance event.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravel means to tangle or knot threads together; oddly the same as unravel in older use.

clue.text: Youthful revellers wiped out after dropping one

indicators.note: wiped out suggests destruction, signalling the letters are rearranged
the fodder's letters lose the letter for one before rearranging

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Young partygoers are exhausted after falling over.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I from REVELLERS WIPED and rearrange the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well-preserved looks younger than their years, keeping a youthful appearance.

clue.text: Worth skipping second ecstasy following hit and draw on this?

indicators.note: following puts the worth word after the word for hit

parts.note: to pip is to strike or beat narrowly

indicators.note: skipping means leaving out the named letter

parts.note: esteem means regard or worth
the second E (ecstasy is E) in the word for worth

explanation.surface: Valuing something less after a drug, a smoker takes a hit and a puff.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the second of the E's in ESTEEM to give ESTEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoker draws on the narrow tube of a tobacco pipe, so this is what you draw on.

clue.text: Trouble man to return flower

indicators.note: returning means the man's name runs backwards

parts.note: Sid is a man's name
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A fellow is going back with a bloom, causing problems.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a calamity, serious trouble or misfortune.

clue.text: All-in wrestling pursued without resistance

indicators.note: wrestling suggests twisting, so the letters are grappled into a new order
without means a letter is removed from the fodder

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Freestyle grappling chased someone who put up no fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All-in wrestling' reads as a sport; 'All-in' alone is the definition. Remove R from PURSUED and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: All-in is British slang for exhausted, having spent all one's energy.

clue.text: Position of university when cutting maths subject

indicators.note: cutting means the university letter slices into the subject's name

parts.note: stats, short for statistics, is a branch of mathematics

explanation.surface: The standing of a college when it drops a numerical course.
explanation.definitionFit: Status means standing or rank, one's position in society.

clue.text: One mum left in Westminster street wants to appear on this

indicators.note: in means the letters for one, mum and left go inside the Westminster street

parts.note: W1 is a London postcode district in the City of Westminster, with 1 read as I
I is the Roman numeral one
to keep mum is to stay quiet, and SH is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A lone mother abandoned in a London street hopes to be listed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not mother but silence, as in keeping mum.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired items, or wants, are what one writes on such a list.

clue.text: Some regularly accepting glory, giving peace to many?

indicators.note: accepting means the regular letters take in the glory word
regularly means every other letter of the word some is taken

parts.note: a halo or glory is a ring of light round a holy head

explanation.surface: Some people often take credit while bringing calm to the masses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrew greeting means peace and is used by many Jewish people, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Minute example of key drink

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A tiny instance of a principal beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt is short for malt whisky, a type of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Having taken two starters each, too full for food

indicators.note: the first two letters of each of the words too and full are taken

explanation.surface: After two courses apiece, diners are too stuffed for anything more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters' looks like first courses but means opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu is bean curd, a soya-based food.

clue.text: Songs circulating around unknown country

indicators.note: around means the turned songs word goes round the unknown
circulating means going round, so the word for songs is turned back

parts.note: airs are songs or tunes
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Tunes going round a mysterious land.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Stand ground

definitions.meaning: a stand or pedestal on which something rests
the foundation or basis of something

explanation.surface: A pedestal resting on the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name a support or footing: a pedestal and a foundation.

clue.text: Half of detailed instructions to make cheese

indicators.note: half of means the second half of the word for instructions is dropped

parts.note: a briefing gives detailed instructions

explanation.surface: Use only part of a recipe to produce cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese.

clue.text: Foundation following peacekeepers around battleground

indicators.note: around means the peacekeepers' letters are turned round

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, provides peacekeeping forces
a field of battle is a battleground

explanation.surface: A charity backs troops near a war zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nuffield Foundation is a British charitable trust funding research and education.

clue.text: Old organ is musical

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ

explanation.surface: An ancient pipe organ produces music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the instrument, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's stage musical based on Dickens's Oliver Twist.
